concepts.name: First Law of Thermodynamics & PV Thermodynamic Processes
concepts.summary: First Law: $\Delta Q = \Delta U + \Delta W$. In isothermal process ($\Delta T = 0$), $\Delta U = 0 \implies Q = W = nRT\ln(V_2/V_1)$. In adiabatic process ($Q = 0$), $PV^\gamma = \text{const}$ and $W = -\Delta U = \frac{nR(T_1-T_2)}{\gamma - 1}$. In isochoric process ($\Delta V = 0$), $W = 0$. In isobaric process, $W = P\Delta V$.
concepts.standard_formulas: \\Delta Q = \\Delta U + \\Delta W, \quad PV^\gamma = \text{const}, \quad W_{\text{iso}} = nRT\ln\frac{V_2}{V_1}, \quad \\Delta U = n C_v \\Delta T
concepts.common_traps: Slope of an adiabatic curve on a $P-V$ diagram is $\gamma$ times steeper than the isothermal curve: $(\frac{dP}{dV})_{\text{adia}} = \gamma (\frac{dP}{dV})_{\text{iso}}$.
concepts.tips_and_tricks: Work done in a cyclic process equals the enclosed area of the loop on the $P-V$ diagram. Clockwise cycle $\implies W > 0$ (Heat engine); Counter-clockwise $\implies W < 0$ (Refrigerator).

concepts.name: Carnot Heat Engine Efficiency & Refrigerator COP
concepts.summary: Carnot engine efficiency $\eta = 1 - \frac{T_2}{T_1} = \frac{W}{Q_1}$ (temperatures strictly in Kelvin). Coefficient of performance (COP) of Carnot refrigerator $\beta = \frac{Q_2}{W} = \frac{T_2}{T_1 - T_2}$. Relation between $\beta$ and $\eta$: $\beta = \frac{1-\eta}{\eta}$.
concepts.common_traps: Substituting Celsius instead of Kelvin temperatures into $\eta = 1 - T_2/T_1$. ALWAYS convert to Kelvin first!
concepts.tips_and_tricks: To double the efficiency of a Carnot engine, it is always more effective to lower the sink temperature $T_2$ than to raise the source temperature $T_1$ by the same amount.

### 2.1 First Law of Thermodynamics & PV Thermodynamic Processes (Thermodynamic Laws)
- **Exam Weightage**: Tested in **18 PYQs** (Very High Yield)
- **Conceptual Summary**: First Law: $\Delta Q = \Delta U + \Delta W$. In isothermal process ($\Delta T = 0$), $\Delta U = 0 \implies Q = W = nRT\ln(V_2/V_1)$. In adiabatic process ($Q = 0$), $PV^\gamma = \text{const}$ and $W = -\Delta U = \frac{nR(T_1-T_2)}{\gamma - 1}$. In isochoric process ($\Delta V = 0$), $W = 0$. In isobaric process, $W = P\Delta V$.

#### Standard Mathematical Formulation
$$
\\Delta Q = \\Delta U + \\Delta W, \quad PV^\gamma = \text{const}, \quad W_{\text{iso}} = nRT\ln\frac{V_2}{V_1}, \quad \\Delta U = n C_v \\Delta T
$$

#### Common Traps & KCET Pitfalls
> ⚠️ **Caution Point**: Slope of an adiabatic curve on a $P-V$ diagram is $\gamma$ times steeper than the isothermal curve: $(\frac{dP}{dV})_{\text{adia}} = \gamma (\frac{dP}{dV})_{\text{iso}}$.

#### Speed Hacks & Problem-Solving Tips
> 💡 **Speed Trick**: Work done in a cyclic process equals the enclosed area of the loop on the $P-V$ diagram. Clockwise cycle $\implies W > 0$ (Heat engine); Counter-clockwise $\implies W < 0$ (Refrigerator).

### 2.2 Carnot Heat Engine Efficiency & Refrigerator COP (Heat Engines)
- **Exam Weightage**: Tested in **10 PYQs** (High Yield)
- **Conceptual Summary**: Carnot engine efficiency $\eta = 1 - \frac{T_2}{T_1} = \frac{W}{Q_1}$ (temperatures strictly in Kelvin). Coefficient of performance (COP) of Carnot refrigerator $\beta = \frac{Q_2}{W} = \frac{T_2}{T_1 - T_2}$. Relation between $\beta$ and $\eta$: $\beta = \frac{1-\eta}{\eta}$.

#### Standard Mathematical Formulation
$$
\eta = 1 - \frac{T_2}{T_1} = \frac{Q_1 - Q_2}{Q_1}, \quad \beta = \frac{T_2}{T_1 - T_2}, \quad T(\text{K}) = T(^\\circ\text{C}) + 273
$$

#### Common Traps & KCET Pitfalls
> ⚠️ **Caution Point**: Substituting Celsius instead of Kelvin temperatures into $\eta = 1 - T_2/T_1$. ALWAYS convert to Kelvin first!

#### Speed Hacks & Problem-Solving Tips
> 💡 **Speed Trick**: To double the efficiency of a Carnot engine, it is always more effective to lower the sink temperature $T_2$ than to raise the source temperature $T_1$ by the same amount.

## Critical Exam Traps & Recurring KCET Pitfalls in Heat and Thermodynamics

### 1. Speed & 80-Second Constraint Management
KCET demands answering 60 questions in 80 minutes (~1.33 minutes per question). The most lethal trap is spending 3+ minutes on long algebraic derivations. Always check for dimensional consistency or option substitution first.

### 2. NCERT & Karnataka PU Board Direct Lines
Over 45% of KCET theory questions are taken directly from NCERT / Karnataka PU Board textbook summary points, margins, and standard exemplar questions. Pay rigorous attention to exceptions (e.g., electron gain enthalpy of Cl vs F, acidic nature of boric acid, non-polar symmetrical geometries).

### 3. Unit Conversions & Prefix Overlooks
Units of molar conductivity (S cm^2 mol^-1 vs S m^2 mol^-1), micro/nano multipliers (10^-6, 10^-9), and centimeter-to-meter conversions in optics and gravitation account for the highest frequency of careless mark losses in KCET.

### 4. No Negative Marking Advantage
Since KCET has NO negative marking, never leave any question unattempted. When down to two options, use dimensional elimination or parity checks to maximize expected score.
